newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares, hesitant for much of the day, were hit at the close, by a weaker Wall Street, dealers said.

The AEX index of the 25 leading shares fell by 3.82 points, or 0.61 percent, to 627.24. Shortly after opening, the index set a new intra-day high of 631.87, but the market proved unable to head towards resistance levels. Instead, for most of the day, the index shuffled just below Friday's close
Traders, however, were not unduly bearish, saying the drawback was a natural reaction to sharp gains on Friday and provided a useful breathing space.

Unilever and Nutricia, by contrast, were among the markets greatest losers. Their shares were down by 3.40 to 295.00 and by 5.30 to 260.50 respectively. Traders commented that the two had been hit by profit-taking in response to their outstanding performances on Friday.

Among few positive signals, the dollar approached a six-week high against the mark and the guilder. Traders said this helped Royal Dutch to stay in positive territory for most of the day. At the close, its shares were unchanged at 290.80.

In a day in which few individual stocks shone, Beter Bed shares debuted and rose 10 cents from its opening level to 30.60. The bedroom furniture chain was rated as an outperfomer in research by Stroeve, who said the shares could happily push towards 35 guilders.
